alignments.note: נָא takes the idiomatic formula the ASV writes for it, here I pray with no object (rule 30).
Jussive verb with its supplied Let frame and subject pronoun, headed on the lexical be; discontinuous around the negative and the particle (rules 17, 25).
Substantival article assimilated into the pointed preposition takes the supplied pronoun one that makes the participle substantival, and heads on it (rules 12, 41).

Relative takes the whole relative expression of whom, the of stating the possessive relation the recasting puts on the relative; headed on whom. The competing reading gives the of to the resumptive suffix on flesh.
Resumptive suffix on בְשָׂרוֹ: two morphemes point at the antecedent and the ASV writes one relative expression for it (rules 22, 43).
Noun with the supplied determiner the, the possession being carried by of whom (rule 15).
Niphal finite verb rendered as an English passive, headed on consumed; discontinuous around half (rule 25).
The waw of the consecutive clause: the ASV recasts the clause inside the relative already opened by אֲשֶׁר and writes no connective for it (rule 14).
Temporal בְּ before the infinitive construct takes when (rule 52).
Infinitive construct with its phrasal particle out, headed on the verb (rule 44).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes he (rule 18).
מִן takes of; the out beside it is the English verb's particle, kept with the infinitive. The competing reading fuses out of on the preposition under rule 24.
Nomen rectum rendered as an English possessive mother's (rule 29).
Suffix takes the possessive his, which determines the possessor (rules 18, 29).

review_notes: The ASV reorders the relative clause ahead of the temporal clause; unit membership follows the Hebrew and the discontinuities are allowed by rule 25.
